title: Dirty Rice Crew Skillet
seoTitle: Dirty Rice Crew Skillet | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Cajun sausage, beef, rice, and vegetables in one pan
subtitle: Cajun sausage, beef, rice, and vegetables in one pan
description: Sausage, ground beef, vegetables, and seasoned rice cook together until fluffy and savoury.

steps.title: Slice sausage
steps.instruction: Slice sausage into coins of equal thickness so each piece browns evenly.

steps.title: Brown sausage
steps.instruction: Cook sausage in a wide deep skillet until its edges colour, then transfer it to a tray.

steps.title: Cook beef
steps.instruction: Brown ground beef in the rendered fat, breaking it into small crumbles and draining if greasy.

steps.title: Verify meat
steps.instruction: Check beef reaches 165°F before it is mixed with the rice.

steps.title: Soften vegetables
steps.instruction: Cook onion, pepper, and celery until soft, scraping browned flavour from the pan.

steps.title: Toast rice
steps.instruction: Stir dry rice for 2 minutes until lightly translucent; do not let it burn on the bottom.

steps.title: Add broth
steps.instruction: Return meats, pour in hot broth and seasoning, then stir once to distribute rice.

steps.title: Simmer covered
steps.instruction: Cover and simmer on low until rice is tender; avoid lifting the lid often.

steps.title: Fluff and hold
steps.instruction: Fluff with a fork and hold covered above 140°F if a call delays dinner.

steps.title: Serve skillet
steps.instruction: Spoon dirty rice into bowls and offer hot sauce rather than over-spicing the whole batch.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover Sausage and beef — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. If tones drop after service, cover hot food and keep sides on low heat or ice as appropriate. On return, spot-check proteins at safe internal temp before reopening the line.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool Sausage and beef and hot components in a shallow baking dish within two hours — food left out too long isn't safe to eat. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Use mild sausage for mixed heat preferences.
Keep the lid tight while rice steams.
Add broth, not water, if rice is underdone.
tonightSpread: Condiments: hot sauce, green onions, pickles
Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Cool Sausage and beef in shallow pans within two hours; label with date and reheat to 165°F before second shift.
Store cold sides separately — hot and cold stacked overnight ruins texture.
whyCrewsLikeIt: It uses economical proteins and one pan, with heat easily adjusted at the table.
mealPrepNotes: Make-ahead: chop vegetables and mix seasoning 2 days ahead. Storage: refrigerate 3 days. Reheating: heat mixture to 165°F.
